findings.detail: The question nearly copies M1-S44-T1. Both have a Claude Code pipeline that auto-commits outputs above a confidence threshold, the same goal (ongoing error rate plus new error patterns) and the same correct answer (stratified random sampling). Two wrong options also repeat. Option B (move all reviewer time below the threshold because high-confidence outputs are proven accurate) repeats the earlier 'send only low-confidence docstrings to reviewers'. Option C (check only rewrites that a later check flags) repeats the earlier 'check only docstrings that developers later report as wrong'. Only option D is new, so more than one wrong option repeats.

blind_answer.reason: Taking a stratified random sample of the merged high-confidence rewrites gives an unbiased, ongoing error rate for each segment and surfaces new error patterns. B stops measuring the high-confidence rewrites altogether. C only sees errors that tests happen to catch. D uses a fixed set that cannot detect new patterns.
